title: Uniform linear loss of sections from powers of a point ideal on a projective curve
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed [def-weil-field], let $C\subset\mathbf P^{r-1}_k$ be a closed subscheme of dimension at most one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $P\in C$ be a closed point lying on a one-dimensional irreducible component. Suppose its homogeneous-coordinate Hilbert polynomial is $\delta m+c$, $\delta>0$ [def-sfb-projective-coordinate-hilbert-polynomial]. Put $L=\mathcal O_C(1)$ and let $\mathcal I_P=\ker(\mathcal O_C\to k(P))$ be the ideal sheaf of the reduced point [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], with powers [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. There exist integers $m_0,K\ge1$, depending on $C$, its embedding and $P$, such that, for every $m\ge m_0$ and every integer $0\le t\le m$,
$$\dim_k H^0(C,\mathcal I_P^t\otimes L^{\otimes m})\le\delta m-t+K.$$
The estimate allows nilpotents, embedded points and disconnected $C$; it requires no nodality or smoothness at $P$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-projective-closed-subscheme-homogeneous-ideal] to the given embedding and write $C=\operatorname{Proj}(B/J)$, $B=k[x_0,\ldots,x_{r-1}]$, with its actual homogeneous vanishing ideal $J$. The vanishing polynomials in each degree already form a vector subspace, so taking their span in [def-sfb-projective-coordinate-hilbert-polynomial] does not change them: the coordinate piece in the hypothesis is $(B/J)_m$. By [lem-sfb-coordinate-quotient-section-polynomial-tail], its canonical section map is an isomorphism for all sufficiently large $m$. The chart formula there identifies its twist with the restriction of the ambient twist, which is $L^{\otimes m}$ by the transition rule of [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. Enlarge one integer $m_0\ge1$ so that for every $m\ge m_0$ the given coordinate polynomial also agrees with the coordinate dimension. Thus $H_m=H^0(C,L^{\otimes m})$ is finite-dimensional and $\dim_k H_m=\delta m+c$. This choice is independent of $t$.

proof.text: Choose a standard chart $x_i\ne0$ containing $P$. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] and the affine characterization in [def-weil-closed-immersion], its intersection with $C$ is $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ for a quotient $A$ of $k[u_j:j\ne i]$, $u_j=x_j/x_i$. It is locally of finite type over $k$. The closed-point residue-field statement [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base] gives $k(P)=k$. Write $a_j=u_j(P)\in k$, $y_j=u_j-a_j$, and $\mathfrak n=\ker(A\to k)$. Then $\mathfrak n=(y_j)$: subtracting the constant term from a polynomial in the $y_j$ expresses it as a sum of multiples of the $y_j$. Put $R=A_{\mathfrak n}$ and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak nR$, using [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The local trivialization of $L$ is $x_i$, and the point ideal and its powers have stalks $\mathfrak m$ and $\mathfrak m^t$, respectively, by [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] and [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers].

source.place: Tag 0AG7 (lemma-recover-tail-graded-module); Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK); Tags 01IN (lemma-closed-subspace-scheme), 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober). Agent explicit chart and jet argument for the estimate in Gieseker Proposition 1.0.3, printed pp.33--34, observations (i)--(iv).

proof.text: Fix $1\le t\le m$. Every class in $R/\mathfrak m^t$ is represented by a polynomial in the $y_j$ of total degree less than $t$. Indeed, if $s\in A\setminus\mathfrak n$, write $s=b+h$ with $b=s(P)\in k^\times$ and $h\in\mathfrak n$. Modulo $\mathfrak n^t$ its inverse is $b^{-1}\sum_{q=0}^{t-1}(-h/b)^q$, because multiplying gives $1-(-h/b)^t$. Thus localization introduces no additional classes modulo $\mathfrak n^t$; subsequently discard all monomials of degree at least $t$. For a remaining monomial $y^\alpha$, with $|\alpha|<t\le m$, the homogeneous polynomial $x_i^{m-|\alpha|}\prod_{j\ne i}(x_j-a_jx_i)^{\alpha_j}$ has degree $m$ and restricts, after division by the basis $x_i^m$, to $y^\alpha$. Its restrictions on all standard charts glue to a section by [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. Consequently the $k$-linear evaluation map $e_{m,t}:H_m\to R/\mathfrak m^t$, defined by taking the germ at $P$ and dividing by $x_i^m$, is surjective. The same monomials show that $R/\mathfrak m^t$ is finite-dimensional.

Let $Z$ be a one-dimensional irreducible component through $P$. By [lem-sc-scheme-sober] it has a generic point $\xi

e0$ in $R$: an equation $sa^j=0$ with $s
otin\mathfrak n$ contradicts primality of $\mathfrak q$ (also for $j=0$). Hence $\mathfrak m^j
e0$. Each $\mathfrak m^j$ is finitely generated by degree-$j$ products of the finite family $y_j$, including $1$ for $j=0$. If $\mathfrak m^j=\mathfrak m^{j+1}$, [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson] applied to this module over the local ring $R$ forces it to be zero, a contradiction. Thus all $t$ successive factors $\mathfrak m^j/\mathfrak m^{j+1}$, $0\le j<t$, are nonzero. They are finite-dimensional subquotients of $R/\mathfrak m^t$. Adding their dimensions along its filtration gives $\dim_k R/\mathfrak m^t\ge t$.

source.place: Tag 0AG7 (lemma-recover-tail-graded-module); Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK); Tags 01IN (lemma-closed-subspace-scheme), 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober). Agent explicit chart and jet argument for the estimate in Gieseker Proposition 1.0.3, printed pp.33--34, observations (i)--(iv).

proof.text: The kernel of $e_{m,t}$ is precisely $H^0(C,\mathcal I_P^t\otimes L^{\otimes m})$, viewed as a subspace of $H_m$. To see this directly, on a trivializing open tensoring the ideal inclusion with $L^{\otimes m}$ is just the ideal inclusion times a free basis. At $P$ its image consists of germs in $\mathfrak m^t$; away from $P$ the ideal of the point is the whole structure sheaf. A section in the kernel therefore belongs locally to the indicated ideal submodule at every point, so its unique local lifts glue. The reverse containment follows on germs. The ideal and power descriptions used here are exactly [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] and [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. Surjectivity from step 3, finite-dimensionality from step 1, and the bound in step 4 now give, for $1\le t\le m$ and $m\ge m_0$, $\dim_k H^0(C,\mathcal I_P^t\otimes L^{\otimes m})=\delta m+c-\dim_k(R/\mathfrak m^t)\le\delta m-t+c$.

proof.text: Choose an integer $K\ge1$ with $K\ge c$. Step 5 proves the desired inequality for $1\le t\le m$. For $t=0$, $\mathcal I_P^0=\mathcal O_C$, so step 1 gives the same inequality. The constants are fixed before $t$ is chosen. Only the existence of a positive-dimensional component through $P$ entered step 4; none of the steps imposed reducedness, connectedness, nodality or smoothness.
